set.presentation: A 52-year-old woman has 8 months of trouble falling asleep. Most evenings, once she lies down or sits through a film, a deep crawling ache in both calves makes her get up and pace the hall; it settles while she walks and returns when she stops. Tired all day; neuro exam and pulses normal.
set.management: A dopamine agonist (pramipexole or ropinirole), long the drug of choice; gabapentin also eases symptoms and a benzodiazepine can improve sleep quality. Opioids are not a routine choice.

set.use: Long-standing drug of choice for unpleasant evening leg sensations that start at rest, force the patient to get up and move, and ease only while walking; gabapentin is a listed alternative

set.presentation: A 19-year-old college student, BMI 22, has fallen asleep in lectures and at meals since about age 15 despite 8 hours in bed; his roommate hears no snoring. Twice, laughing hard at a joke, his knees gave way and he sank to the floor, awake throughout. Exam normal.
set.workup: Overnight study: 1 breathing event/h and no other cause of sleepiness. Next day, five scheduled naps (9, 11, 1, 3, 5): asleep within 1 min each time, and in REM within 3 min in three of the naps.
Overnight study: asleep for 79% of the time in bed; more N1 and less slow-wave (delta) activity than a young adult; REM about 20%; about 15 brief arousals per hour; 3 breathing events/h.
